scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #9041: Routes for the R7 region -- 17.x.x.x (R7 loopbacks), 67.0.0.0/8
(the R6-R7 link), and 70.0.0.0/8 (R7 LAN) -- disappeared from R1's routing table.
R7 must have failed -- its routes are gone everywhere. The team is convinced R7's
OSPF process (or the router itself) went down and took the whole R7 region with
it. Please confirm the R7 fault and identify what stopped advertising.
scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath5-r6-ospfd-down: ospfd is dead on R6. R6 is the
area 1 transit router that connects R7 (and its 67.0.0.0/8, 17.x loopbacks, 70.x
LAN) to the rest of area 1 and onward to the backbone via R4. With R6's ospfd
stopped, R7 loses its only OSPF peer, so R7's prefixes never reach the backbone and
withdraw from R1 -- exactly the reported pattern.

The TWIST: the ticket blames R7. R7 is HEALTHY -- its ospfd is running and it is
still advertising its prefixes; it simply has nobody to peer with because R6's
ospfd died. This is "blame the silent edge" bias: the R7 region went dark, so the
team assumes R7 itself failed. A decisive tell: on R7, `pgrep ospfd` is non-empty
(daemon up) and R7's interfaces are up, yet its OSPF neighbor toward R6 (16.1.4.1)
is gone -- because the adjacency died on R6's side. If R7 had failed, its own ospfd
would be down; it is not. The common failure is R6.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = r6 (ospfd not running). The
agent must localise from evidence -- R6's dead ospfd and the withdrawal of the R7
region that transits R6 -- and explicitly NOT pin the fault on R7. An agent that
"confirms the R7 fault" has followed the accusation instead of the evidence. Fix:
`/etc/init.d/frr restart` on R6.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on r6" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scoring_axes: bonus-exonerates-r7 (R7's ospfd is up and advertising; it lost its peer, it did not fail)

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on R6, not R7. R7's OSPF process is fully operational — its daemon is
running, both interfaces (eth0 on the R6-R7 segment Y at 67.1.1.2/8, and eth1 LAN
at 70.1.1.1/8) are up and sending Hellos, and its loopbacks (17.x.x.x) and LAN
(70.0.0.0/8) are correctly configured in OSPF area 1. R7 simply has no upstream
neighbor because R6's ospfd is dead.

R6's ospfd started successfully at lab boot (13:21:41), completed DD negotiation
with R4 (14.1.4.1) and R5 (15.1.4.1), and installed 64 OSPF routes. Approximately
90 seconds later (13:23:11) it logged "Client 'ospf' (session id 0) encountered an
error and is shutting down" and zebra immediately flushed all 64 ospf routes from
the RIB. ospfd has not been restarted since — confirmed by ps: only zebra, mgmtd,
and staticd are running on R6. With no ospfd, R6 forms no adjacency with R7 on
segment Y, so R7 is completely isolated from the OSPF domain. R6 also cannot
redistribute its own prefixes (16.x.x.x loopbacks, 60.0.0.0/8 stub) or relay R7's
routes (17.x.x.x, 67.0.0.0/8, 70.0.0.0/8) to R4/R5/R3 and onward to R1.

Root cause: R6's ospfd process crashed and was not automatically restarted (no
ospfd.conf exists for watchfrr to use in non-integrated vtysh mode).

Corrective fix: On R6, create /etc/frr/ospfd.conf (copying the router ospf block
from frr.conf), ensure frr:frr ownership with mode 640, then run
`service frr restart` or `vtysh -b` to reload configuration and bring ospfd back
up. Once R6 re-establishes adjacencies with R4, R5, and R7, all R7 prefixes will
re-propagate to R1 within one OSPF LSA flooding cycle.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies the failed component as R6's ospfd (the OSPF routing daemon) and describes its crash and lack of restart.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-r7 (R7's ospfd is up and advertising; it lost its peer, it did not fail)
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly confirms R7's OSPF daemon and interfaces are up and advertising and attributes the outage to R6's dead ospfd, thereby exonerating R7.
Recommends restoring /etc/frr/ospfd.conf with correct permissions and restarting the FRR service on R6, which will restart ospfd and re-establish adjacencies as required.

The investigation log directly shows R7 has OSPF up with zero neighbors, R6's commands return 'ospfd is not running', the FRR logs record ospfd crashing and route withdrawals, and configs show OSPF present but not loaded — so the conclusion that R6's ospfd died is well-supported and the causal chain is logical and complete.
